correctness.rationale: For positive-curvature strictly convex planar C3 boundary and positive continuous density f, local small-arc chord sagitta κℓ²/8 and circular maximum-spacing law on every positive-probability subarc yield (n/log n)^2 E d_H→max κ/f² /8; a global exponential spacing tail supplies uniform integrability. Local missing area κℓ³/12 and beta third circular-gap moment 6/[n(n+1)(n+2)] yield n² E area deficit→(1/2)∫κ/f² ds. Hölder separately minimizes these with f_H=√κ/V and f_A=κ^(1/3)/Z. With µ=f_H ds, q=f/f_H, a=κ^-1/2 and m=Eµ a^(1/3), RH=(min q)^-2 and RA=E(a/q²)/m³. Strict convexity under floor q≥t and ∫q=1 produces the unique water-filled q_t=max(t,c_t a^(1/3)), with strictly increasing F(t)=RA(q_t) for t_A<t<1, meeting decreasing t^-2 uniquely at t*. Its positive open floor and normalized errors balance; circle is the sole R=1 case. Finite ellipse quadrature only corroborates the infinite proof.

originality.rationale: Sonnleitner 2025 states the leading Hausdorff asymptotic for smooth positive boundary densities and the separately optimal √κ law; distinct area-optimal κ^(1/3) law is known. Their separate optimal laws do not imply the exact minimax of max{supremum coefficient, integral coefficient}. A related indexed ellipse result minimizes area versus perimeter, with two integral objectives and a different smooth optimizer. The current curvature clipping and equalizing scalar frontier for all smooth planar convex curves were not found among those prior claims; generic water-filling principles remain a residual possibility.
residual_risks: The constrained water-filling/obstacle minimax functional may be covered abstractly in older optimization literature, though the stated geometric application was not found.
The proof is fixed-density planar smooth asymptotic expectation; finite n, nonpositive curvature, adaptive or sample-size-dependent laws are not covered.

value.rationale: Two separately canonical geometric approximation losses have incompatible density laws. This theorem supplies a unique exact compromise, a qualitative clipping transition, strict noncircular cost, and a practical scalar characterization valid for all positively curved planar bodies. A future researcher choosing a single i.i.d. boundary law to control both errors needs precisely this minimax curve, not simply either separate optimum.

limitations: Planar strictly convex C3 κ>0, fixed continuous f>0, asymptotic expected Hausdorff/area losses only.
No higher-dimensional, adaptive, finite-n optimality or varying-density claims.
